sentences.text: Alan Milburn has said the country needs a "complete system reset" to bring down the number of young people not in work or education - known as "Neets".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: In a major review, published on Tuesday, , external he suggested a raft of proposals to address the problem, which mostly cover England but he says can be adapted in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland too.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Each of his recommendations will need to be accepted by the government and implemented and paid for before they become reality - and that could take some time.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: So how might today's proposals affect you if you are Neet?
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Major report proposes welfare changes, apprenticeships and tax cuts to help 440,000 young people into work At the heart of the recommendations, Milburn says, is a new Youth Opportunity Service.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He wants this to be implemented locally, with each area drawing up a plan to help their own young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: It would bring together employment, careers, health and practical support, with each young person getting a named adviser and a personalised plan.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants areas to begin building their Youth Opportunity Service from 2027, with one in place everywhere by the end of 2029.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within 14 days of entering the service, a young person would then meet with a named adviser.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Within four weeks, they would have their "personalised participation plan", setting out what both the support services and the young person involved would do, and when.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Jobs wise, Milburn wants there to be initiatives like work placements of up to 12 weeks, structured volunteering opportunities, and help to create businesses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants those who remain Neet - despite enagaging with support - to be provided with a paid six-month job, funded by the government.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The government has already committed to a legal guarantee of job support in theory , but the exact workings still need to be worked out.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Alongside more work opportunities, Milburn wants a "major expansion" in further education for 18- to 24 year-olds, as well as more apprenticeship places.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Over the next decade, he wants the number of young people completing an apprenticeship to double, and for apprenticeships to rival university as an option for school leavers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Colleges should also get new funding for participation and work-readiness, the review says, initially targeted at 16- and 17-year-olds who are Neet or at serious risk of becoming so.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: He also wants the government to develop new industry-led technical colleges and specialist campuses.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: If the reforms are enacted, Milburn says young people should have better access to high-quality further education and apprenticeships by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Under the proposals, schools, colleges and universities would be judged by whether pupils make successful transitions into further learning and work, rather than just academic achievements.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: By 2036, he wants 35% of each year group to have started a high-quality apprenticeship by age 25.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The young people caught up in Britain's Neets crisis At a glance: Key proposals from Milburn's Neets report Milburn has said he wants a fundamental transformation of how mental health support for young people is delivered.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Young people who are Neet should be guaranteed fast-track access to services within three months, according to his recommendations.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: This would include things like vocational rehabilitation, talking therapies and counselling as part of a young person's plan with their local Youth Opportunity Service - which would be rolled out between 2027 and 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: There has been a big rise in mental distress among children and young people in recent years, and Milburn's report comes at a time the NHS is facing huge pressures.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants mental health support to be available for all young people digitally, without needing a diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Some areas are already using these approaches, but scaling them up would be a major challenge and would take a long time to introduce across the board.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants "fitness to work" notes to be taken out of the hands of GPs and put into community work and health teams, and for them to be "a trigger for help - not simply a certificate of absence".
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn wants these changes to begin in 2027 and would be linked to the Youth Opportunity Service rollout, which would be complete by 2029 under the plans.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Milburn has said he wants companies to be incentivised to employ more young people, with the report highlighting a competitive jobs market and applicants who often fail to hear back from potential employers.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: The report includes three asks of employers: to create more genuine first jobs, more first-job apprenticeships and much wider access to meaningful work experience.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: Plus, Milburn wants large employers to find ways of responding to rejected job applicants.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: To achieve this, the report suggests a £3,000 payment for employers who take on someone who has been Neet for six months, with a further premium of £2,000 available if they are a small business.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: An extra payment of £2,000 would go to employers taking on somebody taking substantially greater barriers, such as care leavers or disabled young people.
sentences.article_title: Out of work and not in college: How quickly could Milburn's plans help you?

sentences.text: These payments are proposed to be part of changes to the Youth Jobs Grant - which already exists , external - but they would expand under Milburn's proposals from 2027.

sentences.text: Too many university students can use AI to complete assessments without staff finding out, the higher education regulator in England has said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The Office for Students (OfS) said "a significant proportion" of assessments are unsupervised and many can be completed to a high standard with AI, sometimes in minutes.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said this posed a "significant risk" to their credibility, and closed-book and practical exams were the most effective forms of assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK said many institutions had "made substantial changes" to make assessments "AI-proof".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities that do not meet OfS quality standards could soon be banned from charging increased tuition fees or have caps imposed on their student numbers, under proposals that are now being consulted on.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The new research from the OfS and Advance HE, a charity that gives awards for teaching excellence, is based on the views of 244 higher education staff and 91 students from at least 127 universities.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It said "a significant proportion of assessments" were in "unsupervised, non-controlled formats where AI can be accessed by students completing them".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "Many of these can be completed to a high standard using AI tools with limited engagement from students," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: It also concluded it was "frequently possible" for students to use AI "in ways that cannot be reliably detected".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Unsupervised assessment can include coursework, but also remote online exams.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: They were rolled out widely during Covid, and research from Swansea University , external last year suggests 93 universities in the UK still use them in some form.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Josh Fleming, director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said there were "fantastic" examples of universities seizing opportunities presented by AI, but there should be "far greater use of AI-free assessment".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It also presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students' learning and institutions' ability to assess them," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Kathryn Harrison-Graves, deputy chief executive at Advance HE, said students wanted "greater clarity about what is expected of them" but staff had "varying levels of confidence and support".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Some staff, meanwhile, were receiving lots of assignments that looked the same, and did not think their institution's assessments were "fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Other staff described a "polarised atmosphere" between students who used AI and other "conscientious objectors" who avoided it on environmental and other grounds.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: The research said AI literacy for students was important during and after university, and some institutions were clearly communicating to students where AI can and cannot be used in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: But it said there was "an urgent need" to ensure that remote or "non-secure" assessments "maintain their validity despite the availability of AI tools, meaning they effectively assess the knowledge and skills they are designed to measure".
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "If it becomes possible to complete an assessment using AI without the knowledge and skills being tested, the assessment should be replaced," it added.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Universities UK, which represents more than 140 institutions, said universities were "making significant progress" adapting to AI.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "There is further to go but many have made substantial changes to how they assess students.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: This includes more in-person exams, presentations, vivas, process-based assessment and assessments that integrate AI in a controlled way," a spokesperson said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: "It's time to get rid of the outdated methods, that have been kept around in the name of tradition, and instead encourage the innovative practice we see across the sector, co-designed with students based on what they want from higher education," he said.
sentences.article_title: Students passing university assessments in minutes using AI, regulator warns

sentences.text: Pupils will not be allowed access to their phones at all during the school day under stricter government guidance in England.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Statutory guidance came into force in June, making schools and trusts legally responsible for being phone-free throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Ministers now say changes to that guidance will go beyond the current "no see, no hear" policies in place in some schools - where phones can remain in pupils' bags if they are not seen or heard - when it comes into force from September 2027.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But head teachers' unions said schools would struggle to implement stricter new policies without additional funding from government.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the government's "clear message" to parents and pupils was that "school is for learning and friendship, not scrolling".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Access to phones "risks pulling children away from their learning and from each other", the government said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Schools will be able to decide how to follow the guidance.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Some schools have invested in sealed pouches or secure lockers.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Others collect phones at the start of the day, or have prohibited them from sites altogether.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Powell said such policies could achieve a "whole-school culture change" - and that was "what we want to see happening everywhere".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Karl Harrison, head teacher at Burnage Academy for Boys in Manchester, told the programme the school had spent £20,000 to bring in a system of metal detectors and phone pouches to prevent pupils from accessing their phones.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: While some felt their freedom had gone, locking phones away had increased how much pupils socialised at school, he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "People now can talk to each other, instead of scrolling on a device," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: But he said the more robust measures recommended under the new guidance would "come at a cost".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, said the latest guidance "does at least provide some clarity", but added that school leaders "cannot simply make mobile phones disappear".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "If all schools are going to be expected to have lockable pouches or other secure storage facilities for every pupil, the cost involved will be very significant indeed," he said.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "This is not feasible unless the government puts in the funding required to meet these costs." Responding to questions about funding, Powell told BBC Breakfast that she wanted heads to have the autonomy to implement the policies that work best for their schools.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, said she welcomed strong action to stop phones distracting pupils and disrupting the school day.
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: Charlotte Ashton, co-founder of campaign group of Generation Focus, similarly welcomed the changes, saying "no see, no hear" policies were not working and pupils were still "TikToking in the toilets".
sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: "Ultimately, we need to get to a point where it's not normal for every single child to have a personal internet-enabled device in their pockets with them 24/7," she said.

sentences.article_title: Phones to be banned from pupils' bags or pockets under stricter rules for schools in England

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Musicians being 'reskinned' by AI copycats Is this real or AI?
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: It is a question increasingly asked underneath social media videos, and often difficult to tell.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But there is a new trend when it comes to digital manipulation.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Across social media, AI-generated characters are appearing in videos that look remarkably similar to those posted by real people.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: From musicians to dancers and comedians, content creators are finding their performances cloned by these characters that are designed to look funny, realistic, or hypersexualised.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Experts call the practice "reskinning" and say it is made possible by cheap, easy-to-use AI tools.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: People can discover their work has been copied by seeing a video of a character making the same joke or doing the same dance, even with the same background.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Sometimes the AI version has millions more views than the original.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Some of the accounts identified by BBC Verify appear to be using these AI-generated videos to get views and likes, and to eventually make money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Others appear to be experimenting with AI to make people laugh or simply for the attention that comes with going viral.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But the practice has angered content creators who say their original work is being stolen.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Lloyd says videos of her performances have been repeatedly reskinned by accounts that replaced her with over-sexualised AI-generated characters.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: One Facebook account published hundreds of short videos of a guitarist called "Mila Vasari" that had each gained thousands of views.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify found that at least three copied Lloyd's performances and used the exact same music, movements, and even facial expressions.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify did not find any evidence that "Mila Vasari" is a real person.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The videos on the Vasari account also contain visual inconsistencies that suggest AI was used to create them, including distorted fingers playing chords that don't match the music, and guitar strings that fail to move when strummed.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The account, which appears to be run from Canada, did not respond to questions about the purpose of these videos.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Its profile links to a page devoted to Vasari on Fanvue, a subscription platform that allows creators to charge for content, including adult material.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: BBC Verify has found two other accounts fronted by AI-generated guitarists that have reskinned Lloyd's performances and use those avatars to sell and promote adult content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But Lloyd is far from alone in having her content manipulated by AI.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I've got so many messages from other artists and creators that have had the same thing happening to them," says Kjetil Krogstad, a Norwegian content creator known for videos showing him happily dancing in a suit while carrying a cup of tea.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: In March, his followers alerted him to the fact that one of his videos had been reskinned using an AI-generated bunny.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: The post went on to attract millions of views - outperforming Krogstad's original video - before being deleted.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: When Krogstad looked into the account behind the bunny video, he found it promoting courses on how to make money from AI-generated content.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Dr Tina Kendall, an expert in online culture at Anglia Ruskin University, says that while these videos are sometimes made for fun, often the people behind the accounts copy videos that have already proven popular in the hope of attracting audiences and making money.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "What these tools allow people to do is just automatically take a viral concept that's already existing and to reuse it through these reskinning tools," she says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Kendall sees this as part of a wider online "hustle culture", in which accounts seek to turn users' attention and engagement into money - be it through subscriptions to fan pages featuring adult  content, risky cryptocurrency products like meme coins, or monetisation features on social media platforms.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: And making these copies "conventionally attractive, white, feminine" characters can help, Kendall says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I cannot explain how angry I am right now," Grace Roberts, a British car creator, said on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "I put the videos side by side and I could see it was my exact facial movements, how my body moved, the exact same background and even the people around me were completely copied," she told BBC Verify.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "It was just me that had been altered." "I pay for the cars, I build the cars, I pay for the cameras, the filming equipment, and then someone can just hit download on their computer, change it, and then make money off the back of my video," she added.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Her concerns are echoed by other content creators who fear these AI-generated accounts could cost them valuable exposure, followers, and potential income.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: American comedian Julia Jasunas, who called out having her jokes stolen online by AI, said in a recent Instagram video: "The thing that is most concerning is these AI bots are going viral and people think that they're real people.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "And for context, comedians post their stand-up clips online to get you to come out and see live comedy," she said, adding that comedians spent a long time crafting jokes on stage and honing them into punchy lines.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But legal protections are only part of the challenge.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Identifying those responsible for copying the videos, and stopping them from doing it again, can also prove difficult.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Stopping these pirated performances is a game of whack-a-mole, says Alwyn Cruz, who has made a name for himself on social media by exposing AI musicians.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "You don't even know who's making these [videos].
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: And then if you shut it down, they're just going to create another," he says.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: Earlier this week the head of Instagram, Adam Mosseri, said the platform is also "working quickly on ways to catch copies that are harder to spot, like when someone takes scripts or jokes and uses AI to swap out the visuals".
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: But for artists like Lloyd, the damage may already be done.
sentences.article_title: The real people finding their work copied and stolen by AI characters

sentences.text: "It takes years to master an instrument and seconds to take and rip it off as something else - and then people don't even know it's you." What do you want BBC Verify to investigate?

sentences.text: After an eight-year journey travelling almost six billion miles (10bn km), a spacecraft called BepiColombo has arrived at its final destination and is now in orbit around Mercury.

sentences.text: It‘s operating in an extremely hostile environment: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun and temperatures can reach a fierce 430C and then plunge to -180C, and it is constantly blasted with intense solar radiation.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Until now, the planet has been little explored but the hope is this mission will solve some of Mercury's major mysteries.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: "I think it's a little bit of an under-loved planet in the inner Solar System, but I think that's one of the reasons why it is so compelling," said Prof Emma Bunce, from Leicester University, who is a principal investigator on the mission.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: With the spacecraft heading deep into the inner Solar System, it has had to battle the Sun's immense gravitational pull.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: So it has had its brakes on for the entire journey, and has also taken a very convoluted path - looping once around the Earth, twice around Venus and six times around Mercury -  to slow it down enough to get into orbit.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: This journey should have taken seven years, but a problem with BepiColombo's propulsion system meant the already epic voyage was extended by a year.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: The final manoeuvre to get into orbit was a perilous one: a 37-minute handbrake turn that allowed it to be grabbed by the planet's gravity.
sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.article_title: Mysterious Mercury gets a visitor - after spacecraft's eight-year epic voyage

sentences.text: Africa is pushing for adaptation finance to be tripled by 2035, from an annual $40bn (£30bn) In Uganda's northern Karamoja region, Elijah Lobur and his family now eat just one meal a day.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: A severe drought that began in April has destroyed crops, while food brought in from elsewhere has become increasingly unaffordable.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Seven months without rain has brought us to this point where we now live in hunger," the 44-year-old farmer, who lives with his grandmother, wife and five children, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Even some of the wild plants that we used to eat have withered and dried up." Local officials say more than 90% of crops have failed in the region, where agriculture is largely rain-fed.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Further south, in Malawi, Mathews Nkhambala has experienced the devastating effects of flooding.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: In April 2024, barely a year after Tropical Cyclone Freddy devastated the country's southern region, floods displaced people in Chikwawa district.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Nkhambala fled to higher ground with his wife and four children as floodwaters swept through his village.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "As we reached a safe height, we saw our house swept away right in front of our eyes.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Everything I had was gone," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: He lost a harvest of 15 bags of sorghum and part of his farmland.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: His children were so traumatised that they stopped going to school.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "They refused to go to school for many months.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: They were so disturbed," he recalled.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: After relocating and trying to rebuild his life, Nkhambala is now facing another climate challenge - this time a lack of rain.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "This time we fear there may be no harvest.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: I have no clue what I will do." A government assessment after Cyclone Freddy found that Malawi had experienced more than 50 disasters linked to storms, floods, landslides and droughts since 1980, affecting millions of people.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: While Uganda and Malawi are suffering the effects of climate change and their governments are asking for assistance adapting to the new global weather patterns, they are among 23 African countries yet to submit National Adaptation Plans (NAPs) to the UN climate convention secretariat.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: These are the plans that detail how climate change has affected them and the risks they face, and so help make a case for what assistance they need.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Without them, experts say, it becomes difficult to secure funding.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Our region has experienced cyclical droughts for decades, but there has been no action plan to tackle these climate impacts," said Milton Lorpia, who works for Warrior Squad Foundation in Karamoja region of Uganda.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The interpretation of that commitment remains contested.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The proposal was not accepted for formal negotiations at the summit, although African negotiators have continued to push for it.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The funding is intended to help vulnerable countries prepare for and withstand climate change-induced extreme weather, such as droughts, floods and wildfires.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But the European Union, one of the largest providers of climate finance, says the priority should be ensuring existing commitments reach vulnerable countries rather than setting new funding targets.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "We haven't come to the table with additional monies or additional capital.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: It's about what we have committed already and ensuring it's deployed," Darragh O'Brien, who leads the EU delegation at COP31 on behalf of the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU, told a press conference.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: He acknowledged that developing countries faced difficulties accessing available funding, saying the process needed to be improved.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Wopke Hoekstra, the European Commission's climate commissioner, also argued that the summit should focus on delivering existing pledges rather than making new ones.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The scale of the need is substantial.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: According to the UN's Adaptation Gap Report published last year, sub-Saharan Africa requires about $51bn annually in adaptation finance, while the Middle East and North Africa needs $112bn.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Globally, developing countries will need about $300bn annually by 2035, according to the UN's latest report.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Yet they received only about 10% of that amount from developed countries in 2024.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Climate-related loss and damage in Africa is projected to cost $440bn between 2020 and 2030, according to Nairobi-based think tank Power Shift Africa.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Under the 2015 Paris climate agreement, developed countries are required to provide financial support to developing nations, including for climate adaptation.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But why have so many African countries failed to prepare plans that could help them identify their needs and build resilience?
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "If you look closely, the countries that are yet to submit their NAPs are already dealing with multiple crises, including debt distress, economic pressures and other issues," said David Abudho, climate justice lead at the aid agency, Oxfam.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Their governments' ability to invest in climate adaptation is limited." Sheila Apiny, regional climate justice adviser at ActionAid, said the lack of plans reflected a wider shortage of financial and technical support.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "The absence of NAPs in so many countries is, in itself, evidence of an adaptation finance and capacity gap," she argued.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: She said this created a vicious cycle - countries lack support to prepare their plans, while not having the plans makes it harder to secure funding for climate resilience.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "When countries lack adequate adaptation planning and, more importantly, the resources to implement those plans, governments are forced into a cycle of responding to disasters instead of preventing or reducing their impacts," said Amos Wemanya, senior climate adviser at Power Shift Africa.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Instead of investing in early warning systems, climate-resilient agriculture, water security and flood protection, scarce public resources are repeatedly diverted towards emergency relief and reconstruction.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Of course, having a comprehensive NAP helps countries prioritise investments and prepare proposals for climate finance," said Mahlet Eyassu Melkie, a senior strategic adviser to Ethiopia's COP32 presidency.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Fred Njehu, a Pan-African political strategist at Greenpeace Africa, said their absence could nevertheless create significant obstacles.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "It is fair to acknowledge that missing adaptation plans act as a major functional barrier that severely bottlenecks the speed, volume and quality of international funding a country can access," he said.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But having a plan does not guarantee the money needed to implement it.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "Even countries that have completed their NAPs have not received money anywhere near what they require for implementation of their adaptation plans," Apiny said.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Kenya offers an example of how adaptation measures can help communities cope with climate pressures.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: The walls of the sand dams store water underground when the rivers dry up In the country's arid and semi-arid south-east, concrete sand dams slow the flow of seasonal rivers, allowing sand to accumulate and store water underground.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Communities can access it during dry periods using hand pumps or by scooping it out.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: UK charity Sand Dams Worldwide and its local partner, the Africa Sand Dam Foundation, said they had built about 1,300 such dams, improving access to water as droughts become more frequent and intense.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: But many vulnerable communities elsewhere on the continent are still waiting for similar interventions.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Back in drought-hit Karamoja, Lobur wonders how different things might have been if farmers had access to small-scale irrigation schemes.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: "We do have some underground water sources in some places.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: If there were proper plans and programmes, we could have tapped them to grow food, but we are having to live in hunger instead," Lobur said.
sentences.article_title: More climate money for Africa? Europe says use what's already pledged

sentences.text: Bududa has suffered repeated deadly landslides over the years Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: They say the government relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights and livelihoods.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The UN Human Rights Committee is considering what is believed to be the first case seeking  climate adaptation measures, one that could set a global precedent.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: At least 33 of the 53 people who died in the 2019 landslide were children.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: Years later, survivors say every spell of heavy rain brings back fears of another tragedy.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: William Tsama, one of the claimants, lost four members of his family.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: "My quest should be a lesson," he said.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: "Victims in such situations, ignored by governments, can take them to court to compel them to help their citizens." Uganda introduced a resettlement plan for landslide-prone areas in 2011, but progress has been limited, with relatively few people relocated.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: Last month, it launched a new resettlement programme offering affected households 18m Ugandan shillings ($4,300; £3,300) to help them move to safer areas.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: But some survivors have questioned whether the amount is enough to cover the cost of relocating and rebuilding their lives.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: Under the programme, families can choose between receiving two acres of land, valued at 8m shillings, plus 10m shillings  towards building a house, or taking the equivalent land allowance in cash, alongside the same housing grant.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The scheme is expected to benefit 1,410 households identified as living in high-risk areas.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The government has now given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The threat extends beyond landslides.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: The complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also affected farming, leaving many families struggling to secure their livelihoods.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: "I want to get a new good place for my people, so even if I die, they will be okay.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: I am an old man, but I am doing it for my children," Tsama said.
sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.article_title: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN

sentences.text: Pugh said the Strait of Hormuz has an "extraordinary natural world" beneath the surface A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the Strait of Hormuz to draw attention to what he says is the environmental cost of the conflict involving Iran.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Lewis Pugh, who is a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km (9.3 miles) through the strategic waterway, a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Pugh, 56, who was born in Plymouth, Devon said "war causes immense human suffering" but nature is "another casualty that receives far too little attention".
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: He is calling for an end to the fighting, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and action to address environmental damage caused by the conflict.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: The Strait of Hormuz carries a significant share of global oil shipments from the Middle East The swimmer is believed to be the first person to attempt a long-distance swim in the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began in March .
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: He swam from Musandam Island in the strait to the Cape of Hormuz, at the northern tip of Oman's Musandam Peninsula.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: According to the Lewis Pugh Foundation, an oil tanker was struck by a projectile about 4km (2.5 miles) from where he was swimming on the first day.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: On the second day, he saw flames rising above a headland separating him from the burning liquefied petroleum gas carrier Tara Gas and later passed close to the vessel while it was still on fire.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "My immediate thoughts were for the seafarers on board," Pugh said.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "The flames were enormous.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "War causes immense human suffering.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Lives are lost, families are torn apart, and homes, hospitals and schools can be destroyed in minutes," he said.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: "But there is another casualty that receives far too little attention: nature itself.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: And the damage can last long after the fighting has stopped." The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping routes and is also home to wildlife including dugongs, sea turtles and whale sharks.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Pugh said oil spills and other contamination could have long-term consequences for marine ecosystems including coral reefs, seagrass meadows and mangrove forests.
sentences.article_title: Hormuz swim highlights environmental cost of war

sentences.text: Fisher's estuarine moths are highly threatened due to coastal erosion Wildlife enthusiasts have made a record-breaking number of sightings of an elusive moth at a nature reserve.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: The Fisher's estuarine moth has been spotted 111 times at Abbotts Hall in Great Wigborough, near Colchester, in 2026.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: Dr Zoe Ringwood, of Essex Wildlife Trust, said work to boost the highly threatened species' population had been an "important success story".
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: The charity has pledged to continue surveying new and existing plots on the Essex coast.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: Fisher's estuarine moths can be recognised by their pale gold-brown wing colour with light and dark spots, and are naturally found in low-lying areas of natural grassland which are vulnerable to erosion.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: They are reliant on rare hog's fennel for their survival, but the plant has been affected by rising sea levels.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: To protect the species, Essex Wildlife Trust planted hog's fennel at Abbotts Hall in 2005 and introduced moth eggs five years later.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: There is now a self-sustaining population of the moth at Abbotts Hall, according to Essex Wildlife Trust More than 100 of the scarce insect were recorded for the first time in 2025, before the record was broken again in 2026.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: The charity said it was confident there was now a self-sustaining population at Abbotts Hall.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: "[It is] a reflection of how taking evidence-based conservation action can achieve positive results for a threatened Essex species," said Ringwood, its senior conservation evidence manager.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: Hog's fennel has also been planted at nature reserves in Fingringhoe, Wrabness and nearby Tollesbury.
sentences.article_title: Record-breaking sightings of rare moth in Essex

sentences.text: The project aims to create and restore habitats for amphibians and lizards Ponds are to be restored and freshwater habitats created for amphibians and reptiles at two former colliery sites in South Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: The Froglife charity has been awarded nearly £890,000 of Lottery cash to carry out the work in Rother Valley, as well as at sites in North and West Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Kiveton and Dinnington Community Woodlands were originally regenerated through the National Coalfields Programme after the pits there closed in the 1990s.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Sheila Grundry, from Froglife, said staff were "delighted" to work in the area because "freshwater will make a lasting difference for frogs and other wildlife and it's a great way for local people to learn new skills".
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: The £889,761 investment in Froglife's Coalface to Wildspace project will also  help local communities connect with nature, according to the charity.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Dinnington Woodland is one of the sites in Yorkshire which will be a focus of the project The aim of the project across Yorkshire is to create 48 new ponds, improve 93 existing freshwater habitats and establish new "neighbourhood wildlife corridors" like small ponds and bug hotels.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: These "corridors" will act as stepping stones for local wildlife from insects to birds, providing food, shelter and water to improve biodiversity across former industrial sites and help wildlife move between one habitat and another.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Conservationist Andy Goff, project manager in Yorkshire, said the transformation of the sites would be for everyone.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "We want people to engage with the nature that is on their doorstep and wildlife in general," he explained.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "I'm really excited about getting people involved from all over Yorkshire." The Coalface to Wildspace project is funded by The National Lottery Heritage Fund for the next four years, with Froglife having already run similar projects in the Midlands and Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Rother Valley MP Jake Richards said the project was important for the area.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: "These former industrial sites are an important part of our area's history," he said.
sentences.article_title: Wildlife conservation cash targets ex-colliery sites

sentences.text: Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: The Tesla and SpaceX chief executive was the election's top individual donor , giving $446m (£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Democrats won control of both chambers in the US Congress, flipping both swing seats and making historic gains in places that have for decades been controlled by Republicans.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: The election was seen as a bruising defeat for Trump, who has faced pressure over the impact his policies have had on the cost of living in the US.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Musk was speaking virtually , external at the New York Times DealBook Summit, an annual conference hosted in the city attended by major business and political leaders.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: "I'm not Maga," Musk said, referring to the right-wing political movement.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: He added: "I'm not sure what Maga means... if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that." This marks a major shift in tone by Musk, who has previously been seen wearing a Maga hat.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: "I'm not just Maga, I'm dark, gothic Maga," he joked at a Trump rally in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Musk has worn a Maga hat in public on several occasions For several months at the start of Trump's second term in the White House, Musk served as an unpaid "special government employee" and Senior Advisor to the President, leading the Department of Government Efficiency (Doge) to cut government spending.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: In October 2026, the Pentagon named Musk as a co-lead of a future of warfare study called Project Meridian, while he continued to travel with and advise Trump.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Musk went on to say he did not see much for the money he had spent on the Republicans' campaign, though he added that it was likely that candidates would have fared worse without the spending.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: The large number of Republican losses could have implications for Musk and his businesses.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Democrats coming into power in both the Senate and House of Representatives have pledged greater scrutiny of tech companies, including over the building of controversial data centres.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: In Georgia, where SpaceX has data centre operations, the newly elected Democrat governor promised to limit the rollout of the massive buildings , as well as the tax breaks tech companies often get to build them.
sentences.article_title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'

sentences.text: Democratic lawmakers have also suggested that SpaceX, which has gained an estimated $10bn in new government contracts since Trump was re-elected, should be investigated.
