sentences.text: Conservationists say Jersey is an "important refuge" for red squirrels With growing concerns that red squirrels could soon become extinct in England , one Channel Island is a corner of the British Isles where they maintain a stronghold.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: Jersey is home to a thriving red squirrel population, thanks to the complete absence of grey squirrels, which carry a virus deadly to their red cousins.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: Red squirrels are endangered in the UK , with about 120,000 to 160,000 left in the wild and various projects are aiming to boost those numbers.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: There have some strongholds in England , external , particularly islands, and 75% of the British population is in Scotland , external .
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: However, despite not being native to Jersey, Henry Glynn, an ecologist with the National Trust of Jersey, said they "really are iconic for Jersey".
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: He said: "When you speak to people who have come over to visit the island from the UK, a lot of them will say that one of the things they want to do whilst here is to see a red squirrel, because they're so rare and so difficult to see in large parts of the UK.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: "That is actually really special for them." Red squirrels are not native to Jersey, having been introduced in 1885.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: However, Glynn described them as "naturalised", having become "assimilated into the natural environment" over many years.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: The animals have previously featured in Visit Jersey , external tourism campaigns, including one fronted by conservationist Ben Fogle.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: National Trust ecologist Henry Glynn says red squirrel sightings can be a highlight for visitors The National Trust of Jersey said the island wa s an "important refuge" for the red squirrel, where they were " fairly widespread , external ".
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: It said the inland valleys and woodlands were the best places to spot them.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: The species is legally protected, which means it would be a criminal offence to harm them.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: Nina Powell, senior animal carer at the JSPCA [Jersey Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals], said Jersey has a "good population" of squirrels and that "you can see them almost anywhere".
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: While the primary reason for their success is the lack of grey squirrels, Powell said they also thrived "because people look out for them".
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: She said: "A lot of people do support them, put out feeders and stuff like that.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: "Their habitats are decreasing everywhere... but we do have quite a lot of nature reserves.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: "In some places, we've got rope bridges which really help them cross the roads, and our speed limits are quite low, so that helps them as well".
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: Nina Powell from the JSPCA said the red squirrels it comes into contact with can have quite different personalities More news stories for Jersey Listen to the latest news for Jersey She said the JSPCA had handled 50 red squirrels so far this year, including hand-raising eight babies, called kits (kittens).
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: She said: "We want to keep all animals as wild as possible, so we try and be as hands-off as possible.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: "Some of them don't like us... some of them are quite sweet.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: They really do vary in personality." Glynn agreed that their success had come in part because of the efforts of islanders.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: He said: "They're really beloved amongst the local community as well.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: A lot of people put out squirrel feeders or love to see them in the garden.
sentences.article_title: How red squirrels made island their home

sentences.text: "We get lots of reports from people who just want to tell us they've seen them because they're so happy to have them around." Follow BBC Jersey on X , external , Facebook , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: While there is excitement around Anthropic's listing, there is also some concern from investors about its future ability to generate profits in a competitive area.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Yang Wang, a principle analyst at Counterpoint Research, said the central issue was whether it could "keep pace" as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: However, the share sale would give investors "direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity", Wang said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Anthropic was started by seven former OpenAI employees, led by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Dario Amodei has been outspoken about the risks posed by AI, amounting in his view to a possible threat to human existence.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: The company has called for a slowdown in the development of AI, and a greater focus on safeguards while forging ahead with plans to grow quickly and boost its financing through the public markets.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: OpenAI has voiced similar sentiments and delayed its plans to list on the stock market in order to address AI safety concerns.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Technology stocks have lost value in recent weeks following the US midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Democrats, who now control of both chambers of Congress, are expected to be tougher on AI regulation.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Some Democrat candidates opposed the rapid build of data centres required to run AI.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: But Anthropic went ahead with its market listing, despite the market volatility, because it needed to tap into additional funds, said Marta Norton, who heads strategy at investment firm Empower.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: "AI is financially demanding," Norton told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: "The public markets open up the financial spigot a little bit more and so the time has come." Broader anxieties about the AI industry remain.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Competition from low-cost rival models is growing.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: Expensive computer chips, necessary for the industry to operate, are in short supply.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

sentences.text: And the US Federal Reserve is concerned about high AI-related debt being financed through "complex and opaque" structures, according to minutes from its October meeting to discuss interest rates, as well as the high concentration of AI exposure among a small number of firms.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Trailer for new programme detailing Princess Catherine's cancer journey The Princess of Wales has spoken about how "cancer does change you," in a forthcoming documentary called Heal to be shown on the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It changes your body, it changes you physically - but there is a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you," says Catherine in the first glimpses from the documentary, which features her private thoughts on her illness and recovery.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It's clear we're not meant to carry life's challenges alone," says Catherine's voice-over, accompanied by images of other cancer patients and the princess hugging her own family, including Prince William.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "It is often through pain that we realise there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that," she says, once again reflecting the sense of change from her cancer experience.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Kensington Palace shared a photo of Catherine doing the Three Peaks Challenge, ahead of the documentary Catherine has never disclosed what type of cancer she faced, but in March 2024 she revealed that she had a diagnosis of cancer and was receiving chemotherapy .
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: In January 2025 she announced that she was in remission and in the following months began a gradual return to royal duties.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: She has often spoken about her different understanding of life after her illness, and the need to take a more holistic approach to well-being beyond physical recovery.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: The princess has talked about the good days and bad days that followed her treatment - and wanted to dispel the idea that patients could immediately return to how they felt before their illness.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: This documentary, which will be introduced by Kirsty Young, promises to be the fullest and most personal account of that journey, with her own insights into the impact such illness can have and how she found her own healing process.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: She has since returned to working for her charities and earlier this week was in India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony with Prince William, the first time they had travelled together on overseas royal duties since the princess's cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Catherine visited India for William's Earthshot Prize which was hosted in Mumbai - the first time she'd been at the Earthshot awards since 2022 Among the film crew for the documentary, as director of photography, was Will Warr, who has worked with Catherine and her family before.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: His pictures have been used in a video birthday message by Catherine and a Christmas card which showed a relaxed image of the princess and Prince William and their children.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: Catherine was treated at The Royal Marsden Hospital and funds from the distribution of this documentary, which is to be broadcast in other countries, will be paid to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: When cancer patients finish treatment at the London hospital they can symbolically ring a bell.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "I didn't ring the bell," says Catherine, speaking to her brother James Middleton.
sentences.article_title: Catherine talks openly about how cancer changed her in documentary on BBC

sentences.text: "Maybe this is your ringing the bell," he says, about carrying out the Three Peaks Challenge and this documentary about her healing.

sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: It would make business sense to make a shift." TRNSMT has been running since 2017 Several music festivals in Scotland did not go ahead in 2026, repeating a wider pattern across the UK.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: Rebecca Wallace, a lecturer in commercial music at the University of the West of Scotland, believes the cost of living crisis has had an impact on festival attendances.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: "We are living in a time of austerity and people, especially young people, are having to make decisions between, say, going to big gigs or the rest of their social life.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: No-one can pay for anything." However Wallace, who performs as a musician herself and previously worked at DF Concerts when it was holding TRNSMT's famed predecessor T In The Park, also feels the Glasgow Green event struggled to establish a musical identity for itself.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: "The programming of T In The Park was in line with the promoter's tastes, but also in alignment with young people's tastes, and T became this rite of passage for so many young people," she said.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: "It was part of this Scottish identity and had this identity of its own, which I don't think TRNSMT ever really grasped.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: It just did not meet the cultural moment of the time." Biffy Clyro are among the past headliners of TRNSMT TRNSMT launched in 2017, a year after the long-running T In The Park ended following a festival that saw the deaths of two teenagers and a host of organisational problems.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: Unlike T, TRNSMT was based in a city and did not have camping, with Radiohead and Biffy Clyro among the early headliners.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: McConnell told BBC Scotland News that if the festival doesn't go ahead it will be a blow to Scotland's music scene, as smaller stages there - like the BBC Introducing stage - can help emerging acts.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: "There is a cultural loss that would come with this," he says.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: "For better or worse, TRNSMT is Scotland's festival.
sentences.article_title: TRNSMT: What's the future for Scotland's largest music festival?

sentences.text: He has been in big-budget blockbusters like Twilight, Tenet and The Batman, as well as a string of quirky arthouse films - so what clues can Robert Pattinson's past roles give us about what he might be like as James Bond?
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Every actor creates a new James Bond, and Pattinson is one of the best in the business at crafting a memorable character.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: The British actor can be an action man or an anti-hero, a romantic lead or a comic fool.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: He can be granite-faced or goofy, and everything in between.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "I was thinking about what the aspects of James Bond are, and he's done all of those throughout his career," says Paul Tweddle, host of the Heavy Spoilers film podcast , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: He cites Pattinson's performance as a brooding heartthrob in teen vampire franchise Twilight, his suave and quick-witted secret agent in Christopher Nolan's Tenet, the withdrawn and focused title character in The Batman, and the ruthless and manipulative Antinous in Nolan's The Odyssey.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Pattinson has "often been drawn to really dark fare", says Anna Smith, film critic and host of the Girls on Film podcast , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Wouldn't it be interesting to see Bond go a little bit darker?" she suggested to the BBC's World Service.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "But also what he's got, and I'd like him to do more of, is comedy.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: And goodness knows, we need a Bond who can handle humour." Unusually for a James Bond actor, one word that has cropped up frequently is "weird".
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Earlier this month, Pattinson was described as "the weirdest guy in Hollywood" by the Celebrating Cinema podcast , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Pattinson is an actor who makes bold, interesting, risky choices.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: For such a handsome guy, he can bring the weird, and then some," wrote Chris Hewitt in Empire , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "About 0.07 seconds after the announcement, people were already anticipating the weird with his Bond.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Even his blockbuster assignments are more interesting when he lets his inner freak out to play," Lodge added.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "His big, heightened, leeringly villainous turn in The Odyssey is off on its own beam entirely." Associated Press film critic Jake Coyle said , external smaller films like The Lighthouse and High Life show "Pattinson's proclivity for pushing boundaries".
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "He's certainly the funniest and quickest to laugh James Bond we've had in decades," Coyle continued.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Pattinson in Tenet with Himesh Patel (left) and John David Washington (right) Pattinson plays a dapper and enigmatic British agent in Christopher Nolan's time-bending 2020 thriller, as adept at bungeeing off an arms dealer's tower as he is delivering some deliciously dry wit.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Tenet is the obvious one where Nolan's basically doing a kind of James Bond movie." The Times' chief critic Kevin Maher agrees , external : "Pattinson has effectively played Bond already, when he effortlessly inhabited the role of the suave yet nonetheless lethal British spy Neil in Tenet.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "For many observers (including this one) that was the role.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: There was no turning back after Neil." New York Times critic Alissa Wilkinson noted that Pattinson has picked up other "Bond-adjacent" roles.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "The most obvious is Bruce Wayne, a.k.a.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Batman, the wealthy playboy with a lair of tech toys and his own gussied-up automobile," she wrote , external .
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Like Tenet, The Batman proved Pattinson is an expert at action scenes, whether that be jumping off a building or being involved in an explosive car chase with The Penguin.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Batman is a really good example of where he's a withdrawn figure, someone who has his mind focused solely on a task, and I think that's a big part of what James Bond needs to be," Tweddle says.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: However, Pattinson's 007 should be a little less brooding and aloof than his stony-faced Batman and Bruce Wayne.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Although Pattinson plays the villain in Nolan's Greek epic, Antinous's menace and ruthlessness could come in handy when playing Bond, according to Tweddle.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "I think Robert Pattinson also has quite a psychotic side to him, which a lot of the James Bond books delve into - how he's a killer, and he needs to have that side to him," he says.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "What he's done in The Odyssey shows he can be manipulative, and connive and make certain plans, which is what a spy needs to do." Collider's Collier Jennings named , external The Odyssey, along with Tenet and The Batman, as films that show Pattinson is "the perfect" fit for Bond.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "All three roles carry an element that makes James Bond work," Jennings wrote.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Batman has the combat skills and subterfuge you'd need to be a spy of Bond's caliber, not to mention the cutting edge hardware.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Neil has a great grasp on the intricacies of pulling off complex covert operations.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "Antonius walks with a swagger and arrogance that either makes you love him or hate him." Pattinson's current film sees him play real-life NBC journalist Chris Hansen, who carried out sting operations on suspected paedophiles for TV show To Catch a Predator.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: It again demonstrates Pattinson's range as an actor and his ability to take on complex roles - he balances the portrayal of Hansen not as a villain but equally not as a hero.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "He's very much face-to-face with the predators in the room, and he's controlling the situation," Tweddle explains.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "It's very confrontational and demands a certain amount of power.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Being able to control the room like that is also quite transferable to James Bond, and interrogations are a big part of what he does." Pattinson will next be seen playing shape-shifting villain Scytale in the forthcoming third instalment of the epic sci-fi series - directed by Denis Villeneuve.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: The pair's reunion for the next Bond movie is not a coincidence.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: Villeneuve's experience of working with Pattinson on the film may have been the deciding factor when casting James Bond.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "The thing I adore with Robert Pattinson is that when you roll cameras, there's always a certain moment where you have no idea what will happen.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: He is an explosion in front of the camera," the director told Time , external before the Bond casting was announced.
sentences.article_title: Batman to James Bond: The clues about what to expect from Robert Pattinson's 007

sentences.text: "He has an incredible imagination and is a very playful actor, and a very creative actor, always trying to bring new ways of expressing himself and always trying to surprise me." Surprising, bold, weird?

sentences.text: One thing is for certain, Pattinson's James Bond is going to be interesting.

sentences.text: The Games Rating Authority, based in Stevenage, gets to play the games long before release The latest Grand Theft Auto game brings the franchise's trademark violence and adult storytelling to the latest generation of gaming hardware.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But long before its release, examiners at the Games Rating Authority , external (GRA), based in Stevenage, Hertfordshire, got to play the game to decide its appropriate age rating.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: They analysed its content before assigning a PEGI age rating , external of 18, which covers 38 European territories.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But who decides a game is for adults only, and how do they make that decision?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: The Games Rating Authority administers PEGI age ratings on physical games in Europe Video games experience a similar process to films shown in UK cinemas, where examiners from the British Board of Film Classification watch each film before deciding its rating.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: But rating games presents a unique challenge.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Modern games can contain huge worlds that take months to explore.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Some allow players to make their own choices, meaning two people can have vastly different experiences.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Developers first complete a GRA questionnaire disclosing any contentious content and provide at least two hours of footage, along with transcripts of the game's dialogue.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiners study this material, logging timestamps for instances of blood, gore, horror, drug use or bad language.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiner Sadie West is a fan of role-playing video games Lifelong gamer Sadie West joined the GRA believing it would be the dream job: being paid to play games.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "I definitely look at it more analytically when I'm playing here.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: "Since I've started here, I play games a lot less at home, but because I play in such a different way at work to what I'm playing at home, I can still enjoy it." West uses her skills with a controller to explore choices and scenarios that developers may not have captured on video.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "Things like, is there an NPC (non-playable character) that I can go up to, and can I attack them?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Or what happens if my character jumps off a bridge?
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: "Sometimes I die on purpose to see what a character death would look like." Many games, like Grand Theft Auto VI, feature large sprawling worlds for players to explore When playing games in her own time West hates hurting NPCs, but admits at work: "Unfortunately I have to be a bit evil sometimes".
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She will typically play a game for several days, checking for blood, suggestive costumes and potentially exploitative in-game purchases.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: She says: "Once I'm happy that I've seen everything that would impact the rating, I then go through and I write up a report." That report is kept on record, while a version without plot spoilers is shared online for parents and players to read.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.text: Examiners follow strict classification criteria overseen by a panel that includes child welfare experts and psychologists.
sentences.article_title: Who decides that Grand Theft Auto is for adults only?

sentences.article_title: Vinícius Jr sends message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparks appeal

sentences.article_title: Vinícius Jr sends message to Sudan boy who received prosthetic legs after BBC report sparks appeal

sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.article_title: How Windrush children helped shape Wolverhampton

sentences.text: Shark Tank investor Kevin O'Leary is behind a major AI data centre project in Canada that has so far been embraced by legislators.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: As Americans have grown increasingly sour on artificial intelligence (AI) data centre development, Canada's industry leaders are sensing an opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Data centres in Canada looking pretty appealing right now," Lucy Hargreaves, CEO of non-profit policy group Build Canada, wrote on X the day after American voters passed 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives aimed at limiting or preventing data centre development in this month's midterm elections.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: While the number of proposed AI data centres in the US dwarfs that of its northern neighbour, in recent months Canada is being increasingly pitched as a hub for these so-called "hyperscale" projects.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Those in favour argue that Canada's abundant land, natural gas and cold climate make it uniquely positioned to address some of the problems facing US AI infrastructure, from data centres' proximity to populated areas to noise pollution and strain on electricity grids.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "Some of the capital that would have been deployed to build data centres in the US is now more available for Canada," Hargreaves told the BBC in an interview.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "The question really is whether or not we want to go for that." Unlike in the US, pushback to these projects in Canada has been muted - at least so far.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Many are going ahead without significant disruptions, and legislators have openly embraced them without major political consequences.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: At the heart of Canada's AI data centre boom is Alberta, where 90% of all currently proposed sites are set to be built.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The western Canadian province, rich with natural gas deposits, has pitched itself as "North America's destination of choice" for AI data centres, including by offering a "concierge" service for investors to help build these projects at "unparalleled speed".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One of those investors is Kevin O'Leary, the Canadian businessman, TV personality and an ally of Donald Trump, who announced plans this year to build two large AI data centres - one in Alberta and one in the US state of Utah.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: His planned sites, both named Wonder Valley, are being received in very different ways on either side of the border.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Residents in Utah have organised a fierce opposition campaign. , external The pushback led outgoing state senator Stuart Adams to demand in June that O'Leary scale down the project by 75% , external , from 40,000 to 13,000 acres.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Financing for the Utah Wonder Valley data centre is still underway, and it is unclear when - and if - shovels will hit the ground on the project.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The proposed 7,000-acre, 7.5-gigawatt Alberta Wonder Valley project, meanwhile, has received strong backing from both the provincial government and the local municipality.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project is billed as "off-grid" , external , relying on its own power system fuelled by natural gas sourced from the region.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In April, the Alberta government exempted the project from an environmental impact assessment , external , arguing it was unnecessary, though it will still need to obtain permits prior to construction.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: The project was met with only limited opposition at a local town hall earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: One resident, Dan Harms, told Bloomberg in June , external that he saw the economic benefits of the Wonder Valley data centre and that it was being built "out in the middle of nowhere".
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: In an interview with BBC News, Reeve Ryan Ratzlaf, of Greenview Municipality in north-western Alberta, said the project was the "perfect fit" for his rural community, which had been looking for an industrial tenant to fill a resource-rich parcel of land for 13 years.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Some community members have expressed concern about the amount of water needed to cool the proposed site annually, which is projected to be six million cubic metres, or about the size of 2,400 Olympic-size swimming pools.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Ratzlaf argued the amount was a drop compared to the annual flow of the nearby Smoky River, from which the centre would pull water.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: More broadly, he said he believed that economic benefits to the region outweighed potential risks.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "It's a giant warehouse with computer equipment inside," he said, arguing that it was less risky than petrochemical plants that could have been built in its place.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC News, the CEO overseeing both O'Leary projects, Paul Palandjian, said the two were proceeding at an "equal" pace.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: He acknowledged it had become more of a "hot topic" in the US than in Alberta.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: But there are signs public anger towards AI data centres in Alberta has grown in recent months.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Recent public information sessions on provincial AI data centre plans were attended by some furious residents.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "If no one wants this, why are you pushing forward with this?" one resident asked in an August town hall reported on by the Canadian Press , external , held shortly after Alberta announced that Meta would build a C$13bn ($9bn; £6.8bn) AI data centre in the province.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation has also recently sued the government over its decision to override the environmental assessment for O'Leary's Wonder Valley data centre, labelling it "irrational" in court filings.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: This week, the Alberta government proposed legislation that would put restrictions on where data centres could be built in a bid to ease some concerns.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: There are also signs that public cooperation may be fading elsewhere in the country.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: On Saturday, hundreds of protesters gathered in Canada's Atlantic province of Nova Scotia against a proposed AI data centre , external that will be used by technology giant Anthropic.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: But experts say the US backlash offers a cautionary tale for Canada as it tries to capitalise on the AI boom.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "AI is generally not very popular.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: This is both true in Canada and the United States," noted Sean Mullin, a senior fellow at the University of Toronto and former adviser to Canada's prime minister on the national sovereign AI compute strategy.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "I think we could experience some of the same backlashes if we're not thoughtful about it," he said.

sentences.text: The Carney government, which has made reducing Canada's reliance on the US a priority, has framed the development of AI data centres as a matter of national security and sovereignty.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: It has projected that Canada needs to expand its computing capacity 16-fold over the next four years to meet domestic demand.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: "There has been less of these projects happening, and as a result, they've attracted less attention," he said.

sentences.text: Canada has released some high-level guidance on data centre development, which has been co-signed by Anthropic, Meta and other big AI players.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: It calls on data centres to pay for electricity costs, minimise water use and create long-term benefits for the regions they are in.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: If politicians don't tread carefully, Bek MacIntosh, an Alberta resident who has fought a proposed hyperscale data centre in her community, said she believed public discontent could translate into angry votes, like those seen in the US.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: MacIntosh successfully halted a data centre in Olds, Alberta, , external over concerns with its scale, scope and proximity to her home.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: Even after her eight-month battle, she said she was not opposed to all AI infrastructure and believed Canada had the resources and landscape to build them responsibly.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back

sentences.text: But she fears Alberta has opened the door to "the most reckless of reckless developers", and warned that voters might have a "knee-jerk reaction" if provinces don't take care to develop AI data centres responsibly.
sentences.article_title: Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back
